newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Senate rejects death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Senate rejects death penalty.

text.p: Poland's Senate on Saturday rejected a motion to reinstate capital punishment, which had been banned last month by the lower house of parliament.
Thirty-eight members of the 100-seat Senate voted to keep the death penalty off the books, while 26 favoured its reintroduction and four abstained.
The vote by the Senate, which was debating the country's new penal code and the earlier lower-house decision, ran counter to the views of most Poles.
Public opinion surveys have shown that about 60 percent favour retaining capital punishment for the most serious offences, and only 30 percent want it abolished.
Poland hanged its last convicted criminal in 1988, and a moratorium on carrying out executions has since been in force.
When it abolished capital punishment in March, the lower house introduced life imprisonment as the country's maximum penalty.
Before then, 25 years had been the stiffest jail sentence.
